decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach to the rear right tube; all tubes appear in the right workspace. Raise and pitch gradually before descending.
Continue high right-arm approach while aligning the gripper downward with the rear tube axis. Maintain smooth elbow-up configuration.
Finish downward alignment and descend toward the rear tube, using the wrist view to center the open jaws. Stop near grasp height for visual correction.
The wrist view places the tube too far toward the top of the image. Shift along its axis toward the cap and lower slightly before closing.
Close the right gripper on the centered upper body of the rear tube and settle. Retention will be checked during a short lift.
Lift the grasped tube clear of the table and retract slightly, keeping the gripper closed and its current orientation.
Tube remains visible between the jaws. Carry it toward the rightmost rack slot while gradually rotating it upright, maintaining table clearance.
Continue carrying and uprighting the retained tube above the right side of the rack, with small continuous rotations and closed jaws.
Finish bringing the tube upright over the right-front large slot. Keep the tube above insertion height for a final image-based alignment check.
Lower the upright tube toward the right-front slot, making a small inward alignment correction. Stop short of final depth to inspect slot engagement.
Continue a slow vertical insertion into the right-front large opening. Keep the gripper closed until the tube reaches seating depth.
Open the gripper at seating height, then withdraw slightly to inspect whether the first tube remains upright in its slot.
First tube remains in the rack with the jaws open. Withdraw clear and raise the right arm to approach the nearer diagonal tube next.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller translations and rotations. Raise above the second tube and gradually align for its diagonal tabletop orientation.
Continue controlled downward wrist alignment above the second tube, keeping height while the fingers rotate clear of the rack.
Finish orienting the open gripper downward along the second tube, lowering only to a pregrasp height for wrist-camera centering.
Use the wrist view to shift the open jaws toward the tube body and reduce the visible angular mismatch, with a shallow descent.
Center the tube between the open jaws and descend the remaining short distance to grasp height. Adjust yaw slightly using the tube's visible long axis.
Correct the visible tube-to-jaw angular mismatch at fixed pregrasp position, keeping the jaws open before any further centering.
With the tube axis nearly aligned, shift the gripper along and across the tube to center the upper body between the jaws before closing.
Close on the centered body of the second tube and settle at the current grasp pose. Check actual retention on the next lift.
Lift the second tube clear of the tabletop with the right gripper closed. Verify that it follows the jaws before transporting it to the next slot.
The second tube follows the closed gripper. Carry it toward the center-front rack slot while gradually rotating it upright, keeping clearance above the rack.
Continue the smooth right-arm carry toward the center slot, keeping the second tube firmly retained and gradually upright.
Finish uprighting the second tube above the middle-front slot, maintaining separation from the already inserted rightmost tube.
Lower the upright second tube toward the middle-front opening, with a small lateral correction. Stop above final seating depth for inspection.
Insert the second tube vertically to seating height in the middle-front opening. Keep its position and upright orientation steady with the gripper closed.
Release the second tube to settle into the opening, then withdraw slightly to inspect its depth. The tube shifted in the jaws during lowering, so seating needs visual confirmation.
The released tube appears to be tilting rather than seated. Withdraw the open gripper clear of both tubes and inspect their settled positions before attempting recovery.
The second tube is lying across the rack instead of seated. Raise clear and begin orienting for a top-down recovery grasp; avoid contact with the neighboring tube.
Approach above the fallen tube on the rack while rotating toward a downward recovery grasp. Keep the gripper open and well above both tubes.
Continue the elevated recovery approach toward the horizontal tube body. Align the downward gripper with its cap-to-tip direction while staying clear of the upright tube.
Finish downward recovery alignment while moving over the fallen tube rather than the neighboring upright cap. Pause above grasp height to refine centering.
Replan after the continuity rejection with half-sized rotations and a slight retraction/lowering, finishing the downward orientation without advancing farther into the rack.
The fallen tube has shifted forward from the rack. Move above its new position without descending, and realign gradually using the updated wrist view.
Lift straight up with open jaws to ensure the fingers clear the displaced tube and rack before further recovery alignment.
Move clear to the right of the rack above the fallen tube's new tabletop position. Unwind the wrist continuously in the direction that preserves joint-range margin before the recovery grasp.
The prior move executed zero steps. Reduce translation and rotation increments to move away from the tightly folded elevated pose while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Continue the continuous wrist unwind and reposition above the fallen tube to the right-front of the rack, staying above contact height.
Keep the open gripper above the displaced tube while continuing a smooth yaw turn to match its reversed cap direction; no descent yet.
Continue the elevated yaw alignment with the fallen tube, keeping position fixed and jaws open.
Turn the open gripper closer to the displaced tube's cap-up alignment while lowering only a small amount, still clear of contact.
Complete the cap-up alignment over the recovered tube and descend to a pregrasp height, leaving the jaws open for a centering check.
The recovered tube is now centered and aligned. Lower to grasp height while moving slightly toward its cap to grasp the upper body.
Refine the recovery grasp along the tube body, moving away from the cap while lowering only a few millimeters. Keep the jaws open until centered.
Close around the centered recovered tube body and settle before lifting. Keep the other arm stationary.
Lift the recovered tube away from the tabletop and rack, keeping the gripper closed. Check that the tube stays between the jaws before reorienting.
The recovered tube follows the jaws. Begin a slow combined wrist unwind and uprighting motion above the table, carrying toward the center slot without descending.
Continue the elevated, gradual uprighting of the recovered tube with the gripper closed, maintaining clearance from the rack and the inserted tube.
Continue gradual uprighting and wrist unwind of the retained tube, approaching above the center opening with ample vertical clearance.
Finish bringing the recovered tube upright over the center region. Keep it elevated and retained before attempting a carefully aligned insertion.
Approach the center-front large opening with a forward alignment correction relative to the failed attempt. Lower only to pre-insertion height while keeping the recovered tube upright.
